reason: The operator journey is substantially clearer: cohort-scoped navigation preserves context, staffing and submitted forms are separated from canonical valid evidence, closure explains its irreversible consequence, and ambiguous closure reconciles authoritative status while retaining a same-tab recovery marker. Batch release supports a searchable full-cohort review, keeps filtering separate from the submitted snapshot, and discards stale confirmation after uncertain acknowledgements. The supplied mobile diagnostic capture presents specific round counts, missing criteria and honest closed-round escalation legibly. Public mobile composition follows Precision Instrument coherently, with cost and duration immediately stated and pending project approval disclosed. Nevertheless, the actual single-outcome release path still bypasses the stronger acknowledgement/recovery treatment. That consequential inconsistency prevents agreement with the broad world-class question. Missing approved engagement proof, membership workload facts, hosted provider acceptance and Board-approved closed-round remediation further limit the claim; local test success is useful evidence but does not establish observed operator success.

findings.evidence: ReleaseButton uses the generic runAction path, which awaits authorizedFetch and the complete JSON body without a deadline, accepts every HTTP-success response including null/malformed JSON, and turns transport loss into only “Could not release”. ReleaseButton refreshes only on result.ok or released:true. Consequently a committed release with a lost response leaves the stale row and enables retry; a stalled response remains Releasing indefinitely. This actual control is rendered on the dossier and Decisions page (applications/[id]/page.tsx:552; hash/page.tsx:414). The supplied lost/stalled release browser test exercises ReleaseAllButton, not this control.
findings.userImpact: An operator releasing one applicant cannot reliably distinguish completed release from failure, recover from a stalled acknowledgement, or trust the success message after malformed acknowledgement. This is a source-established conditional failure, not an observed hosted incident.
findings.suggestedFix: Give single release a bounded complete-response operation, validate an action-specific receipt, and show explicit unknown outcome with authoritative outcome reconciliation before another release attempt. Cover committed response loss, stalled bodies and malformed success on the actual single-release control.

notVerified: No hosted Clerk/Supabase/RLS/storage/email acceptance or real authenticated operator journey; intercepted fixtures do not prove these integrations.
No observed human task success, assistive-technology session, physical iPhone or macOS Safari testing.
Board-approved closed-round remediation, privacy/retention operations and original-resume policy reconciliation remain outstanding.
Approved actual engagement artifacts and current membership workload commitments remain absent; private visual review is limited to the supplied synthetic diagnostic capture and source.
